newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-DISAPPOINTED HILL READY FOR NEW CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-DISAPPOINTED HILL READY FOR NEW CHALLENGE.

text.p: Damon Hill admitted on Thursday he was hurt and disappointed to learn this week he had been dropped by the Williams team, but said he was determined to win this weekend's Italian Grand Prix and the drivers' world title.

Refusing to reveal the real reason for his sacking but adding that he intended to stay at the top as a Formula One driver, Hill exuded wit and confidence on the eve of opening practice for his Sunday showdown with his Williams team-mate and only title rival, Canadian Jacques Villeneuve.

His demeanour at a press conference was in stark contrast to the mood of the man who is to succeed him at Williams next year, Heinz-Harald Frentzen. The German appeared drawn and serious as he talked, like Hill, for the first time since last Sunday's sensational news from the Williams team.
The 35-year-old Hill, who is within reach of his first world drivers' title, said anyone who wished to know the true reason he was dropped by the team should ask Frank Williams himself.
But he said he was confident the team would be solidly behind him this weekend and give him a fair chance to win the title.

"I've had assurances from Frank Williams and Patrick Head that I will be given equal treatment between now and the end of the season -- and I believe that to be true," he said, thanking the Williams team for all their help in the last six years.
He admitted: "At first, of course, I was very disappointed. I would not be human if I were not. But since then I've had time to think and I've realised that maybe it is time I flew the nest anyway.
"As to the future, to 1997, I've got to say that what has happened has opened up a lot of opportunities for me and I take the view that the world is my oyster at the moment. Anything can happen."

The Briton currently leads Villeneuve by 13 points with just three races remaining, but needs to shake off the concerns about his future and concentrate on the job this weekend if he is to secure the title.

"I have quite a lot to offer, as a racing driver or as anything else. There is no danger of me being out of work. There is plenty of time for me to look and think and I'm happy to look at all the options which might crop up.

"I've got six years experience with the best team in Formula One and I've grown in stature since I joined the team as a test driver. I've got a lot of experience and a lot of knowledge now, but I want a team that has a complete package to offer.

"New twists like this always give you extra motivation to win and there can be no doubting what I can do. I've won seven of the last 13 races and I am leading the championship and I think that speaks for itself."

Hill's jokey mood as he looked at the future was in strange contrast to the sombre face of Frentzen, who looked stunned as he admitted: "It has all happened very quickly and I am not sure what to say yet.
"I think I can do a good job and I should be able to give Michael Schumacher plenty of competition next year. I am looking forward to that."
Frentzen said he was not signed for Williams until this week and admitted he felt difficult and sorry about the Hill situation.
"I feel for him because he is a very fast driver, but this is the way of Formula One," he said.
